title: Spanakopita
subtitle: Greek spinach and feta filo pie
excerpt: Frozen spinach is wrung completely dry, mixed with crumbled feta, eggs, and dill, then layered between sheets of oiled filo pastry and baked until deeply golden and crisp. Spanakopita is one of the great combinations in Greek cooking -- spinach, feta, and pastry baked together.
sourceNotes: Spanakopita appears in Greek cuisine from at least the Ottoman period. It is made across Greece in both large tray-baked form and as individual triangular pastries. The filling is always spinach and feta -- one of the great combinations in Mediterranean cooking.

content.text: The most important step in spanakopita is squeezing the spinach. After defrosting, gather it in a clean tea towel and wring hard. You should extract a cup of liquid. Wet spinach makes the pastry soggy and the filling loose -- there is no fixing it once it is in the tin.

items.prepNote: or use 270g shop-bought filo pastry -- this recipe assumes filo; use flour only if making your own

content.text: Defrost spinach and gather in a clean tea towel. Wring hard to remove as much water as possible -- you should extract a cup of liquid.
Soften onion in 1 tbsp olive oil. Mix squeezed spinach, crumbled feta, eggs, softened onion, chopped dill, nutmeg, and pepper together. Taste -- feta is salty, so add salt carefully.
Brush a 30x20cm baking tin with oil. Layer 8 sheets of filo in the tin, brushing each sheet with olive oil before adding the next. Let the sheets overhang the sides.
Spread filling evenly. Top with 8 more filo sheets, each oiled. Fold in the overhanging edges. Score the top into portions with a sharp knife.
Brush the top generously with oil. Bake at 190°C for 45-50 minutes until deeply golden and crispy.

items.symptom: Filling is wet and the pastry is soggy
items.fix: After defrosting, gather the spinach in a clean cloth and wring hard -- you should remove a cup of liquid.

content.text: Greece. Found in every bakery from 7am. Eaten for breakfast, lunch, or as a snack. The triangular street food version (trigonas) is sold warm from bakeries across the country.
